[Image: a stack of square boxes in the corner of a room.]

Ann stacks these boxes in the corner of the room. All the boxes are the same size.
How many boxes does she use?
reference_items.figure_description:
An isometric drawing shows a stack of identical cube-shaped boxes resting in the corner of a room. Three line segments represent the room's edges meeting at the corner behind the stack: a vertical line extends straight up from the top-back corner of the stack, a line extends down and to the left from the bottom-left of the stack along the floor, and a line extends to the right from the bottom-right of the stack along the floor.

The stack rests on the floor against both walls. The base layer is completely filled, measuring 3 cubes deep along the left wall and 4 cubes wide along the back wall (a 3 by 4 grid of cubes).

A second layer of cubes is stacked on top against the corner in a stepped pattern:
- Along the back wall (row 1, closest to the back wall), the first 3 columns from the left are 2 cubes high, and the 4th column is 1 cube high.
- In the middle row (row 2), the first 2 columns from the left are 2 cubes high, and the remaining 2 columns are 1 cube high.
- In the front row (row 3), the first column on the left is 2 cubes high, and the remaining 3 columns are 1 cube high.

reference_items.stem:
Get to 20 Number Game

Two children, Joan and Herbert, are learning to play a game “Get to 20.” Here are the rules for the game.

GET TO 20
RULES

Pick Tiles: Each player draws three number tiles.

Add Tiles: Each player places the three tiles to make an addition problem with the sum total closest to 20.

For example, here are four ways a player who draws [1] , [4] , and [5] could place the tiles:

  [5] [1]          [4] [5]          [1] [5]             [1]
+     [4]    or  +     [1]    or  +     [4]    or     + [5]
---------        ---------        ---------         + [4]
       55               46               19         -----
                                                       10

This player should choose to show the addition problem
  15
+  4
----
  19
because 19 is the total closest to 20.

Joan and Herbert played the game “Get to 20.”

Joan picked [2] , [7] , and [9] . Herbert picked [1] , [3] , and [6] .

B. What is the addition problem that Herbert could make with his number tiles that gives a total closest to 20? Be sure to include the total.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
